Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:1589-1637), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:20,306-333). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False and the potion's own `use` iterates the enemies (potions.py:188-198)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.AllEnemies passes no single target: PotionModel.IsValidTarget returns `!TargetType.IsSingleTarget()` for a null target (PotionModel.cs:256-263), so the potion resolves over the whole side. The sim models that by leaving `targeted` False (so use_potion passes target=None, combat.py:1621) and letting the potion walk ctx.enemies itself. The set walked is verdicted separately in the guards, because `CombatState.HittableEnemies` (CombatState.cs:142) is `Enemies.Where(IsHittable)` and the sim uses `not is_gone`.

CanonicalVars (protected override, Explo.rationale: `new DamageVar(10m, ValueProp.Unpowered)` -- and OnUse passes BOTH `damage.BaseValue` and `damage.Props` to CreatureCmd.Damage (ExplosiveAmpoule.cs:36), so the Unpowered prop is the load-bearing half rather than decoration: the 10 is not boosted by Strength and not multiplied by Vulnerable, only blocked. The sim passes DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED and DamageCmd.deal skips both modifier passes for it (cmds.py:56-58, `is_powered_attack`). No ascension branch.

OnUse (protected override, ExplosiveAmpo.rationale: C# snapshots `player.CombatState.HittableEnemies` into `targets` and hands the whole LIST to CreatureCmd.Damage (ExplosiveAmpoule.cs:30,36); the sim builds the same snapshot as a list comprehension and loops DamageCmd.deal over it (potions.py:191-198). The snapshot matters and both sides take it before any damage lands, so an enemy that dies to the first hit is still in the list -- and is then skipped by the damage pipeline's own dead check on both sides. Order is Enemies order on both sides. Target-set equivalence is guard N(AoE).

guards.what: N(AoE): `CombatState.HittableEnemies` (CombatState.cs:142) vs the sim's `[e for e in ctx.enemies if not e.is_gone]`
guards.rationale: SETTLED ON THE MERITS, because the two predicates are genuinely different expressions. HittableEnemies is `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)` and IsHittable is `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(CombatState, this)` (Creature.cs:285-299). The sim's filter is `not is_gone`, i.e. `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46), and carries no ShouldAllowHitting term. The two halves settle differently and both settle faithful. (a) The escaped term is the sim modelling a creature C# has already removed from Enemies, so it EXCLUDES the same creatures. (b) The missing ShouldAllowHitting term does not change any observable, because the sim applies the same predicate one level down: DamageCmd.deal opens with `if not hooks.should_allow_hitting(target): return 0` (cmds.py:51-52) before any hook fires, so an unhittable enemy is skipped either way and no listener can tell which layer skipped it. The three C# ShouldAllowHitting implementers the sim ports -- IllusionPower (powers.py:1572), ReattachPower (powers.py:2354) and AdaptablePower (powers.py:3372) -- all go through that same DamageCmd path. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/potion_probes.py aoe-power`): against an Eye with Teeth mid-Illusion-revival, `should_allow_hitting` is False and the sim's filter still keeps it, and Explosive Ampoule changes nothing -- hp 1 -> 1, no powers -- exactly as the C# empty target list would. NOTE: this argument covers DAMAGE AoE only. A potion that applies a POWER to the set does not pass through DamageCmd, and PowerCmd.apply has no should_allow_hitting term at all -- the same probe shows Potion of Binding landing Weak 1 / Vulnerable 1 on that creature. That is the per-unit G(AoE-power) gap on potion_of_binding and shackling_potion.

guards.what: N1: the damage is dealt per-target in a loop in the sim and as one list call in C#
guards.rationale: CreatureCmd.Damage's list overload is the batching form the damage_pipeline seam already audits -- audit/records/seam/damage_pipeline.json steps 17-18 cover the two-loop shape (damage every target, THEN kill the batch) and the sim's per-target resolution. Not re-verdicted here per binding rule 3; recorded so this record's OnUse verdict is visibly resting on that seam rather than silently assuming the loop is equivalent. What is specific to this potion is only the target list and the 10 Unpowered, both of which match.
